parts:
Yes. I’ve started with a **public-facing baseline audit** of the three properties you gave me, plus a first-pass search of what currently surrounds “Orion Fredericks” online.

The important thing I see already is that you **do have a substantial digital footprint, but it currently reads more like an archive than a deliberately structured contemporary identity**. That is actually a useful position to be in before a new content release.

### 1. urlorionfredericks.studiohttps://www.orionfredericks.studio/ — your strongest identity anchor

The site currently introduces you primarily as an **“Elemental Artist”**, followed immediately by your philosophical statement about physical space, perception, primordial experience and “cosmic birth.” It then moves directly into individual works: Gilly, Fata Morgana, Portal/ET, Twins, Le Attrata and Divinatrix. citeturn0view0

That means someone arriving cold gets a fairly clear impression of:

**Orion Fredericks → elemental / experiential artist → monumental sculpture → fire + water + optics + kinetics.**

That's a strong artistic identity. What is much less visible is **Orion in 2026**: the scale of your career, your technical capabilities, fabrication/engineering leadership, current studio practice, Numinous Designs, commissioned work, creative direction, production capabilities, and what you're working toward now.

There are also some content/SEO issues. The homepage has no real H1 in the indexed version, several project names are abbreviated (“Fata,” “ET,” “Divi,” “Attrata”), and the project descriptions don't consistently contain the search vocabulary somebody looking for your kind of work would use. citeturn0view0turn0search13

So I would **preserve the artistic voice but substantially strengthen the information architecture.**

### 2. Facebook — useful archive, but shouldn't define the new release

urlThe Art of Orion Fredericks on Facebookhttps://www.facebook.com/TheArtofOrionFredericks/

Facebook is throttling external access, so I can't responsibly claim I've audited every post on the page yet. Search also isn't surfacing the page particularly strongly.

For the content strategy, I'd therefore treat Facebook initially as an **archive/community distribution channel**, rather than the canonical source for your identity.

There may be years of useful historical material there that should be selectively resurfaced. The question shouldn't be “How do we restart Facebook?” so much as:

**What valuable material exists there that should become part of the larger Orion Fredericks archive/story?**

That distinction will matter.

### 3. YouTube has potentially much greater strategic value

urlOrion Fredericks on YouTubehttps://www.youtube.com/@OrionFredericks

Direct external crawling of the channel is also being throttled, so I don't yet have a reliable inventory of every video, title and description.

But YouTube should probably become a **primary pillar of the new release**, rather than merely somewhere old documentation lives.

Your work has something photographs can't adequately communicate: **scale, sound, movement, flame, water, audience reaction, fabrication and transformation.**

There is also already video content elsewhere associated with your name. For example, your Vimeo documentation of *Fata Morgana* describes the optical system and the 28-foot projected light body in considerable detail. citeturn1search0

That suggests an opportunity to consolidate scattered moving-image documentation around the YouTube identity.

---

## The more interesting discovery: Google already knows an older version of Orion

Searching your name produces a surprisingly coherent historical record.

MAKE has a substantial 2014 profile titled *The Heavy Metal of Orion Fredericks*, describing you as a Bay Area artist best known for large-scale sculpture. citeturn0search10 Burning Man's own Journal identifies *Fata Morgana* and other projects associated with you, including your contribution to Oakland's Bike Bridge. citeturn1search8turn1search13 The Crucible still has an artist page carrying essentially the same philosophical statement that appears on your present website. citeturn0search12

There are also unusually valuable institutional references. Sotheby's documented **Le Attrata by Margaret Long and Orion Fredericks**, including its turbine-driven blast furnaces and sculptural concept. citeturn0search6 Chatsworth separately describes you and Margaret as artists working with sophisticated flame effects at the intersection of thermodynamics and art. citeturn1search11

And entity["point_of_interest","AREA15","Las Vegas, NV, USA | 3215 S Rancho Dr, Las Vegas, NV 89102"] currently identifies **Mini, Nilly & Hilly** as Orion Fredericks works on its public art page. citeturn1search17

Those are strong third-party credibility signals.

But there's also **digital archaeology competing with your present identity**.

An old Weebly site is still indexed prominently and describes you as an Oakland sculpture artist, with older biographical information. citeturn0search1 Older Burning Man-era pages point toward the obsolete **orionfredericks.net** domain. citeturn1search15turn0search12 Engineered Artworks currently lists you simply as a **“Fire Technician,”** which is accurate to a particular relationship but obviously represents only a narrow slice of your overall practice. citeturn0search11

And now there is another identity entering search results:

urlNuminous Designshttps://www.numinousdesigns.com/ identifies you as **Co-Founder**, describes your Crucible/THERM background, and positions you as someone creating monumental work for more than 25 years. citeturn0search2turn1search9

So the current footprint roughly looks like this:

**1999–2010**
Orion → fire artist / Oakland / Crucible / THERM / Burning Man / Fata Morgana.

**2010–2020**
Orion → established large-scale sculptor / fire + water + kinetics / Maker Faire / festivals / collaborations / Le Attrata.

**2020–2025**
The public narrative becomes much thinner.

**2025–2026**
Numinous Designs begins introducing a new identity: Orion as co-founder / senior artist / monumental fabrication practitioner.

That missing bridge is probably the central problem your new content release should solve.

## I would build the audit around one question

Rather than asking simply **“What content do I have online?”**, I think we should determine:

> **What does the internet currently believe Orion Fredericks is—and what do we want it to understand five minutes after encountering the new body of content?**

Then we can deliberately connect the **35-year arc of artist → builder → technical specialist → creative director → studio founder → mentor/educator**, without abandoning the strange elemental artistic identity that makes the work distinctive. memcite

### Next audit pass

I'd expand this substantially before we decide what you should release. Specifically, I'll map **Google/search results, Google Images, Vimeo, Instagram, Burning Man, MAKE, The Crucible, Maker Faire, AREA15, Sotheby's/Chatsworth, Numinous Designs, old domains/sites, interviews, press, collaborators' sites, and unattributed/misattributed project imagery**.

Then we can sort everything into four useful buckets: **Amplify / Update / Archive / Suppress or supersede**.

That will give us a real **Orion Fredericks Digital Footprint Map**, and from that we can design the release sequence rather than just starting to post new material randomly.

I think the drawing material can solve an important problem in the footprint: it can **introduce the present-day Orion before you begin releasing the heavier historical archive**.

I would categorize it primarily as **ORION — NOW**, secondarily as **ORION — ARTIST**. I would *not* package it primarily as “drawing content” or as generic timelapse/social-media material. The interesting story is that drawing is part of your current creative process and gives people access to the hand and mind behind the monumental work.

### The package I would build

Think of one drawing session as a **content package**, not one video.

| Asset | Length / format | Purpose | Where |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **Hero process film** | 2–5 min, horizontal | Shows the drawing developing and establishes your current practice | **YouTube + website** |
| **Timelapse** | 30–90 sec | Visually satisfying complete transformation | **YouTube Shorts / Instagram / Facebook** |
| **Process clips** | 10–30 sec | Individual moments: mark-making, details, hands, tools, decisions | **Shorts/Reels/social** |
| **Finished drawing** | High-res still | Gives the work authority as an artwork rather than just content | **Website + social** |
| **You + drawing** | Still or short video | Connects the work to *you* | **Website/About + social** |
| **Detail images** | 3–6 crops | Shows texture and visual language lost in timelapse | **Website/carousel** |
| **Short statement** | 50–150 words | Explains why you're drawing now and its relationship to the larger practice | **Website + YouTube description** |

The key distinction is that **the long video is the source material; the individual posts are derivatives**. Don't make yourself invent six different pieces of content.

### Where it belongs on orionfredericks.studio

I would introduce a new section rather than burying these drawings among Gilly, Portal, Divinatrix, etc.

Something like:

**WORK**  
Sculpture  
Drawing  
Experiments / Studies  
Collaborative Work

And eventually:

**PROCESS**  
Studio  
Drawing  
Fabrication  
Testing / Prototyping

The finished drawings belong under **Drawing**. The videos belong primarily under **Process**, with selected process video embedded into individual drawing/project pages.

That distinction becomes important. **Artwork is the result; process is how you got there.**

### YouTube should be the permanent video home

urlOrion Fredericks on YouTubehttps://www.youtube.com/@OrionFredericks should become the canonical moving-image archive.

I wouldn't title videos generically:

> Drawing Timelapse #4

Instead, establish a recognizable series:

> **Drawing the Numinous — No. 01 | Orion Fredericks**

or

> **Studio Studies — No. 01 | Drawing Process**

or simply:

> **Drawing Study 01 — Orion Fredericks**

The description can then connect the drawing to your broader work:

> A drawing study from the current studio practice of sculptor Orion Fredericks, exploring forms and visual relationships that recur throughout my work in sculpture, light, fire, water and kinetic installation.

That connection is doing important digital-footprint work. Someone finding the drawing video isn't left thinking, **“Oh, he's doing drawings now.”** They're shown that the drawings are another window into the same practice.

### Facebook has a different job

urlThe Art of Orion Frederickshttps://www.facebook.com/TheArtofOrionFredericks/ shouldn't necessarily receive the exact same content in the exact same form.

There I'd use a strong finished image or a 30–60 second transformation and a more personal caption explaining what you're doing.

The objective is **reconnection**:

> I've spent a lot of time drawing again lately. These studies have become a place to explore some of the same forms, tensions and spatial relationships that have run through my sculptural work for years...

Then video.

That begins connecting the people who knew you from Gilly/Fata Morgana/Burning Man/Crucible/etc. with what you're doing **now**.

### And this suggests a release sequence

I wouldn't open the new content campaign with a 25-year retrospective.

I'd start **present tense**.

**Drawing → Drawing → Studio/process → Current sculpture → Historical connection → Drawing → Major archival work → Current project.**

For example:

**Week 1:** Drawing process — *here is what I'm making now*  
**Week 2:** Another drawing + finished image  
**Week 3:** Studio/process footage  
**Week 4:** Drawing form → older sculpture that shares the visual language  
**Week 5:** Gilly / Fata Morgana / Portal archival story  
**Week 6:** New/current Numinous work

Now the archive isn't nostalgia. It becomes **evidence of a continuous practice**.

And that's the larger opportunity I see in the drawing footage: **use the quiet, intimate scale of drawing as the doorway into the enormous body of work behind it.**

Yes. I’ve started with a **public-facing baseline audit** of the three properties you gave me, plus a first-pass search of what currently surrounds “Orion Fredericks” online.

The important thing I see already is that you **do have a substantial digital footprint, but it currently reads more like an archive than a deliberately structured contemporary identity**. That is actually a useful position to be in before a new content release.

### 1. urlorionfredericks.studiohttps://www.orionfredericks.studio/ — your strongest identity anchor

The site currently introduces you primarily as an **“Elemental Artist”**, followed immediately by your philosophical statement about physical space, perception, primordial experience and “cosmic birth.” It then moves directly into individual works: Gilly, Fata Morgana, Portal/ET, Twins, Le Attrata and Divinatrix. citeturn0view0

That means someone arriving cold gets a fairly clear impression of:

**Orion Fredericks → elemental / experiential artist → monumental sculpture → fire + water + optics + kinetics.**

That's a strong artistic identity. What is much less visible is **Orion in 2026**: the scale of your career, your technical capabilities, fabrication/engineering leadership, current studio practice, Numinous Designs, commissioned work, creative direction, production capabilities, and what you're working toward now.

There are also some content/SEO issues. The homepage has no real H1 in the indexed version, several project names are abbreviated (“Fata,” “ET,” “Divi,” “Attrata”), and the project descriptions don't consistently contain the search vocabulary somebody looking for your kind of work would use. citeturn0view0turn0search13

So I would **preserve the artistic voice but substantially strengthen the information architecture.**

### 2. Facebook — useful archive, but shouldn't define the new release

urlThe Art of Orion Fredericks on Facebookhttps://www.facebook.com/TheArtofOrionFredericks/

Facebook is throttling external access, so I can't responsibly claim I've audited every post on the page yet. Search also isn't surfacing the page particularly strongly.

For the content strategy, I'd therefore treat Facebook initially as an **archive/community distribution channel**, rather than the canonical source for your identity.

There may be years of useful historical material there that should be selectively resurfaced. The question shouldn't be “How do we restart Facebook?” so much as:

**What valuable material exists there that should become part of the larger Orion Fredericks archive/story?**

That distinction will matter.

### 3. YouTube has potentially much greater strategic value

urlOrion Fredericks on YouTubehttps://www.youtube.com/@OrionFredericks

Direct external crawling of the channel is also being throttled, so I don't yet have a reliable inventory of every video, title and description.

But YouTube should probably become a **primary pillar of the new release**, rather than merely somewhere old documentation lives.

Your work has something photographs can't adequately communicate: **scale, sound, movement, flame, water, audience reaction, fabrication and transformation.**

There is also already video content elsewhere associated with your name. For example, your Vimeo documentation of *Fata Morgana* describes the optical system and the 28-foot projected light body in considerable detail. citeturn1search0

That suggests an opportunity to consolidate scattered moving-image documentation around the YouTube identity.

---

## The more interesting discovery: Google already knows an older version of Orion

Searching your name produces a surprisingly coherent historical record.

MAKE has a substantial 2014 profile titled *The Heavy Metal of Orion Fredericks*, describing you as a Bay Area artist best known for large-scale sculpture. citeturn0search10 Burning Man's own Journal identifies *Fata Morgana* and other projects associated with you, including your contribution to Oakland's Bike Bridge. citeturn1search8turn1search13 The Crucible still has an artist page carrying essentially the same philosophical statement that appears on your present website. citeturn0search12

There are also unusually valuable institutional references. Sotheby's documented **Le Attrata by Margaret Long and Orion Fredericks**, including its turbine-driven blast furnaces and sculptural concept. citeturn0search6 Chatsworth separately describes you and Margaret as artists working with sophisticated flame effects at the intersection of thermodynamics and art. citeturn1search11

And entity["point_of_interest","AREA15","Las Vegas, NV, USA | 3215 S Rancho Dr, Las Vegas, NV 89102"] currently identifies **Mini, Nilly & Hilly** as Orion Fredericks works on its public art page. citeturn1search17

Those are strong third-party credibility signals.

But there's also **digital archaeology competing with your present identity**.

An old Weebly site is still indexed prominently and describes you as an Oakland sculpture artist, with older biographical information. citeturn0search1 Older Burning Man-era pages point toward the obsolete **orionfredericks.net** domain. citeturn1search15turn0search12 Engineered Artworks currently lists you simply as a **“Fire Technician,”** which is accurate to a particular relationship but obviously represents only a narrow slice of your overall practice. citeturn0search11

And now there is another identity entering search results:

urlNuminous Designshttps://www.numinousdesigns.com/ identifies you as **Co-Founder**, describes your Crucible/THERM background, and positions you as someone creating monumental work for more than 25 years. citeturn0search2turn1search9

So the current footprint roughly looks like this:

**1999–2010**
Orion → fire artist / Oakland / Crucible / THERM / Burning Man / Fata Morgana.

**2010–2020**
Orion → established large-scale sculptor / fire + water + kinetics / Maker Faire / festivals / collaborations / Le Attrata.

**2020–2025**
The public narrative becomes much thinner.

**2025–2026**
Numinous Designs begins introducing a new identity: Orion as co-founder / senior artist / monumental fabrication practitioner.

That missing bridge is probably the central problem your new content release should solve.

## I would build the audit around one question

Rather than asking simply **“What content do I have online?”**, I think we should determine:

> **What does the internet currently believe Orion Fredericks is—and what do we want it to understand five minutes after encountering the new body of content?**

Then we can deliberately connect the **35-year arc of artist → builder → technical specialist → creative director → studio founder → mentor/educator**, without abandoning the strange elemental artistic identity that makes the work distinctive. memcite

### Next audit pass

I'd expand this substantially before we decide what you should release. Specifically, I'll map **Google/search results, Google Images, Vimeo, Instagram, Burning Man, MAKE, The Crucible, Maker Faire, AREA15, Sotheby's/Chatsworth, Numinous Designs, old domains/sites, interviews, press, collaborators' sites, and unattributed/misattributed project imagery**.

Then we can sort everything into four useful buckets: **Amplify / Update / Archive / Suppress or supersede**.

That will give us a real **Orion Fredericks Digital Footprint Map**, and from that we can design the release sequence rather than just starting to post new material randomly.

Yes. These files fill in several of the biggest holes in the first-pass audit.

The most important correction is that your footprint shouldn't be reconstructed primarily from what Google currently finds. Your **resume/CV + site inventory establish the authoritative chronology**, and the public web becomes evidence showing which parts of that chronology are visible, missing, distorted, or outdated.

### What the files change

Your current resume establishes three very useful professional eras: **Orion Fredericks Studios (1999–2019)**, **Lumen & Forge (2019–2022)**, and **Numinous Designs (2024–present)**. It also documents that the middle period wasn't an artistic disappearance: at Lumen & Forge you were working in industrial design/fabrication, projection mapping, immersive environments, AR/VR, domes, and experiential projects for clients including Nike, Toyota, McLaren x Mastercard, Don Julio, and Travis Scott x Air Jordan. fileciteturn0file0L21-L45

That's a **major missing chapter in the public narrative**.

Your older CV also proves that the career isn't just “Burning Man fire sculpture.” It documents a long exhibition history from the late 1990s through 2019, including Maker Faire, EDC, The Crucible, Chabot Space & Science Center, Lightning in a Bottle, private commissions and other exhibitions. fileciteturn0file1L12-L30 The public-installation history also includes *Fata Morgana*, *Passage of Awakening*, *Tapasya* and *Springwater*. fileciteturn0file1L77-L83

And your resume pushes the technical history even further back: teaching metalworking at The Crucible, helping build its industrial-arts facility, fabrication for Archie Held Studios, extensive work for Michael Christian/Xian Studios, glass fabrication, foundry/furnace work, controls, fuel systems and structural fabrication. fileciteturn0file0L65-L94

### The spreadsheet may be the most strategically important file

It contains roughly **70 identifiable bodies of work/projects**, rather than the handful represented prominently by the current website.

More importantly, you've already begun doing the curatorial work. There is a priority hierarchy:

**Portal #1 → Gilly #2 → Divinatrix #3 → Twins #4 → Fata Morgana / Le Attrata #5 → Springwater #6 → XOD #7 → Thermokraken #8 → Skrillex #9 → M548A fire-fighting vehicle #10 → Dragonfly #11**, followed by Momentary Realization, Oracle, Opulent Temple, Sanctuary, Supafroopy, Tapasya, Willy, SCM, Harmonizer, Echevaria, Cyclone, Altar of Hang and Bike Arch.

That is extremely useful because I don't think the next release should attempt to publish everything equally.

There's also a remarkable amount of source material already catalogued: image folders, existing copy, videos, collaborators, dates, availability and third-party documentation. Projects such as *Portal, Gilly, Divinatrix, Fata Morgana, Le Attrata, Springwater, XOD,* and *Twins* already have enough material to become substantially richer digital records.

## A clearer picture of the footprint is emerging

I would now divide your digital identity into **five strands**, rather than treating everything as one portfolio:

**ORION — THE ARTIST**  
Portal, Gilly, Divinatrix, Fata Morgana, Twins, Springwater, Tapasya, Echevaria, Momentary Realization, drawings, glass and early sculptural work.

**ORION — THE ELEMENTAL/EXPERIENTIAL DESIGNER**  
Fire, water, optics, thermodynamics, kinetics, sound, lighting and human interaction.

**ORION — THE BUILDER / TECHNICAL LEAD**  
The Crucible, Michael Christian projects, Sanctuary, M548A firefighting vehicle, Dragonfly, Opulent Temple, large fabrication projects, controls, rigging, structural fabrication, fuel systems.

**ORION — IMMERSIVE / EXPERIENCE WORK**  
The Lumen & Forge period: projection mapping, domes, AR/VR, experiential environments and major commercial projects. Your resume explicitly documents this expertise. fileciteturn0file0L133-L139

**ORION — NOW**  
Numinous Designs, current sculpture, commissions, fabrication leadership, Numo/new work, teaching/mentorship and the next phase of the studio. Your current resume positions Numinous as a multidisciplinary studio serving public, civic, corporate and private clients. fileciteturn0file0L5-L20

That last strand is currently the weakest online, despite being the one that should tell people **what to do with you now**.

### There's also an important attribution problem to solve

Your spreadsheet identifies a substantial body of work where you participated in fabrication/design/engineering but the web's canonical page belongs to someone else—for example Michael Christian projects such as *Almost, Bike Arch, Bloom, Brainchild, Candelaphyte, Koilos, Corpus, Epod, Hypha,* and others.

Those shouldn't simply be mixed into “Works by Orion Fredericks.”

Instead, I'd create a clearly identified category such as:

**Selected Collaborative & Fabrication Work**

with your **specific role** attached to every project.

That simultaneously gives you credit for decades of high-level work **without muddying authorship**.

### And the 2020–2024 “gap” isn't really a gap

It's a **visibility gap**.

The files show a progression more like:

**1994–1999 — Formation**  
Glass, ceramics, metal, Alfred, early public sculpture.

**1999–2007 — Crucible / industrial arts**  
Studio building, teaching, fabrication, early fire/water experimentation.

**2002–2010 — Elemental experimentation**  
Thermokraken, Oracle, Twins, Springwater, Cyclone, Fata Morgana.

**2010–2019 — Monumental practice**  
Portal, Gilly, XOD, Divinatrix, Le Attrata, festival/public work and extensive collaborative fabrication.

**2019–2022 — Immersive technology**  
Lumen & Forge, projection, domes, AR/VR and branded experiential work.

**2023–2024 — Re-emergence / new language**  
Drawings, SCM, Dragonfly, Supafroopy and renewed personal work.

**2024–present — Numinous**  
Studio founder, monumental sculpture, technical leadership and new work.

That is a considerably more interesting story than the one the internet currently tells.

## What I think we should do next

I would **not start releasing content yet**.

We now have enough information to build a proper **Digital Footprint Matrix** with one row for every meaningful project/persona and columns for:

**Project → Year → Orion's Role → Authorship → Images → Video → Existing Website → YouTube → Facebook → Third-Party Coverage → Search Visibility → Current Copy → Priority → Action**

Then each item gets one of four actions: **AMPLIFY, BUILD, UPDATE, or ARCHIVE**.

That matrix will tell us something very valuable: **which 10–15 pieces of content can most efficiently reshape the internet's understanding of Orion Fredericks before we start feeding it dozens of new posts.**

And I suspect *Portal, Gilly, Divinatrix, Fata Morgana, Le Attrata, Numo/current work, the Lumen & Forge chapter, and a carefully presented “35 years of making” chronology* will form the backbone—but I'd like the audit to establish that rather than assuming it. memcite

Yes. I’d use this as a **gap-filling worksheet**, not a rating of the work itself. Your files already establish deep fabrication/technical experience and a long exhibition record; what is missing is consistent metadata that lets us confidently place each item into the five-part framework. fileciteturn0file0L29-L45 fileciteturn0file1L12-L30

| Category | What we already know | Information you should add | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Orion — Artist** | Strong sculpture history, exhibitions, public installations | **Authorship:** Sole / Co-created / Fabrication for another artist. **Concept/story.** Year created. Current owner/location. Current status. | **HIGH** |
| **2. Elemental / Experiential Designer** | Fire, water, optics, kinetics, thermodynamics, interaction | For each project: **What is the experience? What does the audience do/see/feel?** Which elements: Fire / Water / Light / Sound / Kinetic / Interactive / Optical. | **HIGH** |
| **3. Builder / Technical Lead** | Extensive fabrication, controls, fuel systems, structural work, teaching | **Your exact role** on every collaborative project: Design / Engineering / Fabrication / Lead Fabricator / PM / Flame FX / Controls / Installation / Safety. | **VERY HIGH** |
| **4. Immersive / Experience Work** | Lumen & Forge, projection mapping, domes, AR/VR, branded experiences | Project names, **what you personally did**, client, dates, images/video you're permitted to show, team credits, technical challenge. | **VERY HIGH** |
| **5. Orion — Now** | Numinous Designs, current studio practice and existing portfolio | Current projects, commissions, works available, services offered, current studio capabilities, **what you want to be hired for now**, new work in development. | **CRITICAL** |
| **Career chronology** | Strong 1990s–2019 history | Better documentation for **2019–2024 transition** and 2024–26 work | **HIGH** |
| **Project metadata** | Many projects named | Dimensions, materials, year, location, collaborators, commissioner/client, exhibition history | **HIGH** |
| **Media inventory** | Spreadsheet contains links/media references | Best 5–10 photos per project, hero image, fabrication images, finished video, press-quality assets | **HIGH** |
| **Press / validation** | MAKE, Popular Mechanics, NYT, SF Chronicle etc. listed on resume | Exact article URL, date, project mentioned, quote/description, publication-quality image | **MEDIUM** |
| **Commercial availability** | Some known | Available / Sold / Permanent installation / Commissionable / Rebuildable / Archive only | **HIGH** |
| **Narrative importance** | Some priority ranking exists | Why each piece matters in the evolution of your practice | **MEDIUM** |
| **Rights / permissions** | Mostly unclear | Photographer credit, video owner, client NDA/restrictions, permission to publish | **HIGH** |

The biggest gaps aren't really **“what did Orion make?”** We already have quite a lot of that. The biggest gaps are **“What exactly was Orion's role?”**, **“Why does this project matter?”**, and **“Can we publish the material?”** Your resume demonstrates just how broad the technical side is—fuel/water systems, controls, kinetics, structural fabrication, machining, CNC, thermodynamics and fluid dynamics—but those capabilities aren't yet consistently connected to individual projects. fileciteturn0file0L113-L139

### The fields I'd add to your existing inventory spreadsheet

Rather than creating a separate database, I'd extend the spreadsheet you uploaded with these columns:

**Primary Category** | **Secondary Category** | **Authorship** | **My Role** | **Year Designed** | **Year Built** | **Client/Commissioner** | **Collaborators** | **Dimensions** | **Materials** | **Elemental Systems** | **Interactive?** | **Concept / Why It Matters** | **Current Location** | **Current Status** | **Available?** | **Best Hero Image** | **Video** | **Fabrication Documentation** | **Press/External Validation** | **Photo/Video Rights** | **Website Status** | **YouTube Status** | **Facebook Status** | **Release Priority** | **Missing Information** | **Next Action**

And I would make **Primary Category** a controlled choice from:

**ARTIST · EXPERIENCE · TECHNICAL · IMMERSIVE · NOW**

A project can have secondary categories, but forcing one **primary identity** will keep the new website/content architecture from becoming muddy.

For example, *Fata Morgana* might be **ARTIST** primary / **EXPERIENCE** secondary; *Sanctuary* could be **TECHNICAL** primary / **EXPERIENCE** secondary; Lumen & Forge projects could be **IMMERSIVE** primary / **TECHNICAL** secondary; and Numo would likely be **NOW** primary with **ARTIST + EXPERIENCE + TECHNICAL** secondary classifications.

The older CV is particularly valuable here because it gives us dates and exhibition history for many works that can populate otherwise empty records. fileciteturn0file1L34-L75

**The first information I'd have you fill in is not dimensions or materials.** I'd start with just four columns for every important project:

**MY ROLE → AUTHORSHIP → WHY THIS MATTERS → CURRENT STATUS**

Once those four are populated, I can categorize the whole body of work much more accurately and identify exactly which pieces should lead the new content release.

I think the drawing material can solve an important problem in the footprint: it can **introduce the present-day Orion before you begin releasing the heavier historical archive**.

I would categorize it primarily as **ORION — NOW**, secondarily as **ORION — ARTIST**. I would *not* package it primarily as “drawing content” or as generic timelapse/social-media material. The interesting story is that drawing is part of your current creative process and gives people access to the hand and mind behind the monumental work.

### The package I would build

Think of one drawing session as a **content package**, not one video.

| Asset | Length / format | Purpose | Where |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **Hero process film** | 2–5 min, horizontal | Shows the drawing developing and establishes your current practice | **YouTube + website** |
| **Timelapse** | 30–90 sec | Visually satisfying complete transformation | **YouTube Shorts / Instagram / Facebook** |
| **Process clips** | 10–30 sec | Individual moments: mark-making, details, hands, tools, decisions | **Shorts/Reels/social** |
| **Finished drawing** | High-res still | Gives the work authority as an artwork rather than just content | **Website + social** |
| **You + drawing** | Still or short video | Connects the work to *you* | **Website/About + social** |
| **Detail images** | 3–6 crops | Shows texture and visual language lost in timelapse | **Website/carousel** |
| **Short statement** | 50–150 words | Explains why you're drawing now and its relationship to the larger practice | **Website + YouTube description** |

The key distinction is that **the long video is the source material; the individual posts are derivatives**. Don't make yourself invent six different pieces of content.

### Where it belongs on orionfredericks.studio

I would introduce a new section rather than burying these drawings among Gilly, Portal, Divinatrix, etc.

Something like:

**WORK**  
Sculpture  
Drawing  
Experiments / Studies  
Collaborative Work

And eventually:

**PROCESS**  
Studio  
Drawing  
Fabrication  
Testing / Prototyping

The finished drawings belong under **Drawing**. The videos belong primarily under **Process**, with selected process video embedded into individual drawing/project pages.

That distinction becomes important. **Artwork is the result; process is how you got there.**

### YouTube should be the permanent video home

urlOrion Fredericks on YouTubehttps://www.youtube.com/@OrionFredericks should become the canonical moving-image archive.

I wouldn't title videos generically:

> Drawing Timelapse #4

Instead, establish a recognizable series:

> **Drawing the Numinous — No. 01 | Orion Fredericks**

or

> **Studio Studies — No. 01 | Drawing Process**

or simply:

> **Drawing Study 01 — Orion Fredericks**

The description can then connect the drawing to your broader work:

> A drawing study from the current studio practice of sculptor Orion Fredericks, exploring forms and visual relationships that recur throughout my work in sculpture, light, fire, water and kinetic installation.

That connection is doing important digital-footprint work. Someone finding the drawing video isn't left thinking, **“Oh, he's doing drawings now.”** They're shown that the drawings are another window into the same practice.

### Facebook has a different job

urlThe Art of Orion Frederickshttps://www.facebook.com/TheArtofOrionFredericks/ shouldn't necessarily receive the exact same content in the exact same form.

There I'd use a strong finished image or a 30–60 second transformation and a more personal caption explaining what you're doing.

> I've spent a lot of time drawing again lately. These studies have become a place to explore some of the same forms, tensions and spatial relationships that have run through my sculptural work for years...

Then video.

That begins connecting the people who knew you from Gilly/Fata Morgana/Burning Man/Crucible/etc. with what you're doing **now**.

I wouldn't open the new content campaign with a 25-year retrospective.

I'd start **present tense**.

**Drawing → Drawing → Studio/process → Current sculpture → Historical connection → Drawing → Major archival work → Current project.**
